decisions.choice: Encode a deterministic store-plus-attempt invoice reference into Authorize.net invoiceNumber and refId within the 20-character limit: 8-hex SHA-256 store tag, a single '.', then the Commerce attempt id (max 11 chars). Characters are limited to Authorize.net-safe [A-Za-z0-9._-]. Creation fails closed on overflow or invalid chars (never truncate). After HMAC-SHA512 verification, receiveAuthorizeNetWebhook parses the reference and rejects (no transactionId write, no wake/alarm, no paid lookup) when the store tag does not match the URL siteId and the stored attempt site. Malformed or legacy bare attempt ids are rejected with no writes. A signed webhook still never marks paid; only authoritative getTransactionDetails lookup does.

decisions.rationale: v1 scope is refunds by hand; automatic refunds risk refunding the wrong payment. decisions.choice: Payments serves its own page at payments.dinkuskit.com/v1/pay/authorize-net/{siteId}/{sessionId} and returns it as the session's redirectUrl. The session Commerce sees never changes: for new sessions sessionId is a stable unguessable Payments id (attempt id plus 128 random bits), not the Authorize.net token, with the same redirectUrl, createdAt and expiresAt on every call, because Commerce refuses a changed session. Sessions already open keep their old token shape until they expire. When the shopper opens the page, Payments checks the checkout: paid, past expiresAt or unknown sends the shopper back to the store; otherwise it mints a fresh getHostedPaymentPageRequest token for the same attempt, amount and store-bound invoice reference and auto-submits it to Authorize.net by POST. The page takes no input, holds no card data (SAQ-A), never puts the token in a URL, and is not cached. Every try from any token carries the same invoice reference, so lookups, webhooks and the every-try-counts rule (payments#95) are unchanged; a shopper paying in two tabs at once falls under payments-authorize-net-paid-twice-044. Requests send duplicateWindow=0 so a declined shopper who fixes CVV or ZIP can retry at once. A checkout whose tries are all unpaid stays open (lookup returns open) until expiresAt; expired-unpaid is returned only once every try is unpaid and both expiresAt and the last minted token's 15-minute life plus a 5-minute margin have passed. Fraud holds (FDSPendingReview, FDSAuthorizedPendingReview) and any other unrecognized status stay unknown, never unpaid. Commerce does not change. Hosted Worker change only; deploy with --keep-vars on a quiet beta, on Ronald's go.

decisions.question: How does an Authorize.net shopper reach the card form for the whole 30-31 minute checkout window, when Authorize.net needs a POST and its form token lives only 15 minutes?
decisions.rationale: Authorize.net docs (developer.authorize.net Accept Hosted): the form is opened by an HTML POST of the token and the token is valid for 15 minutes. Minting on visit keeps Commerce's bounded 1800-1860 s window honest without changing the port. A Payments-owned page is the only place that can POST without Commerce knowing the provider. Re-minting makes a second paid try on one checkout more reachable, which 044 already handles by recording both and telling the owner to refund one by hand.
